assumptions: Source-backed identity: compare desired active-drug amount with the labeled supply amount for the same drug and scale the corresponding liquid quantity.
Application profile: formulation is homogeneous and concentration remains fixed in the withdrawn portion. D and H have exactly matching active-moiety definitions.
Population scope: general prescription arithmetic illustrated by nursing exercises; no therapeutic validation for an age, pregnancy state, condition or route is claimed.

gaps: Need labeled_active_drug_reference_mass, labeled_liquid_reference_volume and prescribed_liquid_medication_volume meanings and m^3 unit; reuse prescribed_drug_mass_per_administration from b01/r2. No runtime projection.
Known inventory density relationship uses bulk mass_density rather than active-drug concentration; no duplicate ID is asserted because the quantity definitions differ.

models.inverse_notes: Target D: V>=0, H>0, Q>0 give D=V*H/Q uniquely. Check V=7.5e-6 m^3, H=0.0004 kg, Q=5e-6 m^3 gives D=0.0006 kg and forward V=7.5e-6. V=0 gives D=0 uniquely. Target H: D>0, Q>0, V>0 give H=D*Q/V>0. Target Q: D>0, H>0, V>0 give Q=V*H/D>0. Retain original guards and formulation context. With D=V=0, H and Q remain underdetermined positive values; with D=0,V>0 there is no solution. With D>0,V=0 no finite positive H,Q can satisfy the identity. Inverting does not authorize changing a prescription or stock formulation.
limitations: Does not select a dose, stock strength, dilution, syringe or rounding policy; no clinical limits are inferred from educational examples.
Cannot use bulk solution density for H/Q, or use added diluent volume as final stock volume when reconstitution changes volume.
The source includes tablet and liquid examples; this record serializes the liquid-volume interface only and preserves other profiles as overlap notes.

references.method: Published 0.5 mL normalized to 5e-7 m^3 for prescribed 25 mg and labeled 50 mg/1 mL. Source result preserved; arithmetic-only 1e-16 m^3 tolerance because this is an exact pedagogical proportion, not a measured syringe volume.
Published 0.75 mL normalized to m^3 for 1.5 mg desired and 2 mg per 1 mL supply. Uses the explicit algebra in the answer, not an uninspected label image. Arithmetic-only tolerance.
Independent synthetic portion argument: one 5 mL portion holds 400 mg and another half portion holds 200 mg, so 600 mg occupies 7.5 mL. Tolerance covers binary arithmetic only.
references.provenance: Curator-constructed stock-portion check, not observed clinical data.

rejection_cases.reason: Zero stock active-drug amount cannot define the required positive concentration.

relationship.locator: Chapter 14, Alternate Formula for Solving Medication Dose Problems; Sample Exercise 14.3
relationship.original_equation: Desired Amount / Dose on hand x Volume = Dose (liquid quantity)
relationship.translation_notes: Preserve source D and H; introduced Q renames the source stock Volume to avoid collision with introduced output V (source liquid Dose). D,H are active-drug mass in kg, Q,V liquid volume in m^3. Normalize mg to kg and mL to m^3 before reference entry; expression D*Q/H has no conversion coefficient. Dimensions: M*L^3/M=L^3; runtime mass scale cancels. H/Q is constituent active-drug mass concentration, not bulk solution density: the building-energy inventory's generic density relationship concerns total substance mass and is not a compatible unqualified binding. Tablet counts are treated as an alternate desired-over-have profile in deferred notes, not another record created solely by unit spelling. Input D carries the weight-based-prescription context shared with clinical-arithmetic--weight-based-prescribed-mass, marking it as the independently authorized per-administration mass that record computes.

sources.evidence: Scales labeled liquid volume by desired mass relative to labeled mass; example gives 0.5 mL and another gives 0.75 mL.

models.summary: Converts an already specified active-drug mass into the corresponding volume of one labeled liquid formulation. It is a proportional amount identity; neither choosing an amount nor deciding to administer it is included.
models.title: Liquid medication volume from prescribed mass and labeled strength

variables.context: Same patient, drug/active-moiety mass basis, independently authorized prescription and one administration. Application profile: actual measured body mass is the independently authorized basis. The prescribed coefficient is per kilogram per administration, not per day or per time. Source examples are pediatric; the arithmetic has no drug-specific clinical validation population.
variables.definition: Active-drug mass already specified for this single administration on the same labeled active-moiety basis as H.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative; zero is the no-amount arithmetic boundary, not a prescribed therapy.

variables.context: Same independently authorized single administration, active drug/moiety and homogeneous liquid stock at its labeled concentration. The supplied reference mass H and volume Q describe the same final formulation. Source is nursing calculation education, not age-specific drug validation; patient eligibility and prescription appropriateness are external.
variables.definition: Mass of the specified active drug contained in stock reference volume Q; not total formulation mass.
variables.domain: Finite strictly positive labeled reference mass; same moiety/salt-equivalent convention as D.

variables.context: Same independently authorized single administration, active drug/moiety and homogeneous liquid stock at its labeled concentration. The supplied reference mass H and volume Q describe the same final formulation. Source is nursing calculation education, not age-specific drug validation; patient eligibility and prescription appropriateness are external.
variables.definition: Final liquid formulation volume containing labeled active-drug mass H.
variables.domain: Finite strictly positive; final homogeneous formulation, not diluent volume before reconstitution.
variables.source_symbol: Introduced Q maps to stock Volume in D/H x Volume

variables.context: Same independently authorized single administration, active drug/moiety and homogeneous liquid stock at its labeled concentration. The supplied reference mass H and volume Q describe the same final formulation. Source is nursing calculation education, not age-specific drug validation; patient eligibility and prescription appropriateness are external.
variables.definition: Unrounded liquid volume containing D under the specified stock mass-to-volume proportion.
variables.domain: Finite nonnegative proportional volume. Device resolution, available stock count and administration decisions are not outputs.
variables.source_symbol: Introduced V maps to liquid Dose/Quantity for dose
